newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Gold-Price rise could rattle hedges.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Gold-Price rise could rattle hedges.

text.p: Australian gold miners may be poised to unwind further forward positions if the market shows signs of rebounding following a steady fall in the gold price in the last 10 days, analysts said on Wednesday.
The higher the gold price the more attractive the idea of unwinding hedges becomes.

Gold has been falling for 10 days straight and was fixed at a fresh two-month low of US$382.45 an ounce in London on Tuesday. Now, some analysts believe, the precious metal is oversold and ripe for an upside correction.
Failure of the price to advance, though, would likely leave most forward positions intact.
The challenge for Australian miners is pinpointing the the top of the next cycle and act ahead of any price retreat.
Australian miners are encouraged by lenders to sell forward their production and reduce their exposure to the marketplace.
Most exposure to gold on their part is generally through gold derivative products and the percentage of output unhedged, which is typically less than half.

Under the buyback strategy, miners would realise net profits by closing out existing gold positions. At that stage they would probably either look to reinstate the selling higher up or use the cash to buy put options to provide short-term cover.
But whether miners are planning to iniate such a strategy in the near future is unclear.

There have been no indications of gold miners closing out large positions since Newcrest Mining Ltd in August said it had unwound two million ounces. This was preceded by a series of close-outs in May, led by Placer Pacific Ltd.
Placer Pacific closed-out 700,000 ounces, following the lead of its 75 percent-parent Placer Dome Inc, which closed out 1.7 million ounces.
Miners may be holding on to positions in anticipaton of prices going lower if IMF gold is sold into the market to raise funds for loans to the world's poorest countries.
The IMF board meets on Friday to decide whether to endorse the controversial proposal.

IMF management, backed by the United States, Britain and most other member nations, has proposed selling around five percent of the fund's more than 100 million ounces of gold to help finance its Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF).
Such an endorsement has the potential to knock gold back to its nearby technical support mark of $380.00, traders said.
"That's probably not a bad level to buy," one said.
While gold has not dropped that far, in Australian dollars, the price already is attractive.
The Perth Mint on late on Wednesday was quoting spot gold at A$479.55 an ounce. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
